rationale: Clinical and genetic characterization of spinocerebellar ataxia 52 (SCA52, OMIM #621535) demonstrates that heterozygous pathogenic variants in RAB3A (most notably the recurrent p.Arg83Trp hotspot) manifest across the overlapping ataxia-spasticity spectrum. Patients consistently exhibit progressive cerebellar ataxia accompanied by upper motor neuron signs, mild lower limb spasticity, and tremors, making differentiation from autosomal dominant spastic ataxias and complicated hereditary spastic paraplegias (such as SPG7 or SPG11) impossible on bedside motor examination alone. Neuroimaging consistently demonstrates cerebellar cortical atrophy with vermian accentuation without severe primary spinal atrophy, which serves as a necessary imaging biomarker to distinguish SCA52 from pure spastic paraplegias and prioritize RAB3A on multi-gene panels.

evidence.text: In two families with cerebellar ataxia and a screened cohort of 320 SCA patients, individuals harboring the heterozygous RAB3A c.247C>T p.(Arg83Trp) variant presented with adult-onset cerebellar symptoms, gait spasticity, and tremors. Brain MRI consistently demonstrated cerebellar atrophy with vermian accentuation, and neuropathology revealed diffuse cerebellar cortical degeneration.

evidence.text: Systematic review of neuroimaging patterns across spinocerebellar ataxias emphasizes that selective or predominant cerebellar atrophy is helpful in narrowing differential diagnoses from disorders characterized by olivopontocerebellar or extensive spinal cord involvement, though no single MRI pattern is entirely pathognomonic on its own.

new_directions.question_text: What quantitative spinal cord cross-sectional area thresholds on volumetric MRI reliably discriminate SCA52 from primary complicated hereditary spastic paraplegias like SPG7?
new_directions.rationale: While brain MRI captures vermian atrophy in SCA52, systematic measurement of cervical and thoracic cord atrophy across SPG7 and SCA52 cohorts will establish objective imaging biomarkers.

new_directions.question_text: Does the presence of co-occurring neurodevelopmental delay or cognitive involvement delineate non-R83W loss-of-function RAB3A variants from typical adult-onset SCA52 R83W missense cases?
new_directions.rationale: Initial studies indicate unique de novo loss-of-function variants present with childhood-onset neurodevelopmental features, suggesting a genotype-phenotype divergence that could refine diagnostic prioritization.
